cards.a: SSM builds distribution trees rooted directly at a specific source (S,G) with no RP, no shared tree, and no register process; receivers use IGMPv3 to join (S,G) and PIM builds a shortest-path tree from the source.

cards.q: What group address range does SSM use?
cards.a: SSM operates in the 232.0.0.0/8 range per RFC 4607; receivers join specific (S,G) pairs in this range, while groups outside 232/8 use standard ASM behavior.

cards.q: What are the differences between ASM (PIM-SM) and SSM?
cards.a: ASM uses any-source (*,G) with a required RP, a shared tree, and a register process, while SSM is source-specific (S,G) with no RP, no shared tree, no register, and only a shortest-path tree.
IGMPv3 is required because it supports include/exclude source lists and lets a host report a specific (S,G) pair, whereas IGMPv1/v2 only support any-source (*,G) joins.

cards.q: How does an SSM join and tree build work?
cards.a: A receiver sends an IGMPv3 (S,G) report to the DR, the DR sends a PIM (S,G) join toward the source, and the source builds a shortest-path tree directly to the receiver with no shared-tree phase.

cards.q: What are the benefits of SSM?
cards.a: No RP, no shared tree, no register overhead, immediate shortest path with lower latency, simpler inter-domain multicast without MSDP, and source authentication since only the specified source is joined.

cards.q: Which command enables SSM for the default group range?
cards.a: The command is ip pim ssm default, which enables SSM for the 232.0.0.0/8 range; ip pim ssm range can be used to specify a custom range.
show ip mroute, show ip mroute ssm, show ip pim interface, show ip igmp groups, and show ip ssm; because there is no RP, show ip pim rp mapping is typically empty.

cards.q: A host cannot create an (S,G) join in an SSM deployment; what is the likely cause?
cards.a: The host is running IGMPv2 instead of IGMPv3, so it cannot report a specific (S,G); set the access interface to ip igmp version 3.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between SSM and PIM-SM?
cards.a: SSM is source-specific (S,G) with no RP, shared tree, or register process, operating in 232/8, while PIM-SM builds (*,G) shared trees through an RP with a register and SPT switchover.

cards.q: What is the SSM quick-review summary?
cards.a: SSM is the no-RP model using source-specific (S,G) joins in the 232.0.0.0/8 range, requires IGMPv3, builds only shortest-path trees, and simplifies inter-domain multicast by eliminating the shared tree and register.
